title: Introduce sampled epochal latency atlas and top-k hotpath detector
author: Maya Chen
ci_status: pass (flaky test rerun after lint fix)
release_notes:
- Add sampled epochal latency atlas reporter for compact distribution storage and visualization
- Add top-k hotpath detector to identify kernel+token hotspots contributing to p99/p999
- New example workloads and e2e benchmark to validate sampling fidelity vs storage cost
description:
Motivation: Our existing reporters capture latency quantiles and heatmaps but store large traces or coarse aggregates that make long-term trend analysis and root-cause attribution expensive. This PR introduces a sampled epochal latency atlas (compact, per-epoch histograms with context stratification) plus a top-k hotpath detector that extracts the most impactful kernel/token paths contributing to long-tail latency. The design aims to keep storage and ingest cost low while preserving signal required for regression detection and debugging.

Design summary: The atlas reporter samples requests at configurable epoch intervals (epoch == N requests or fixed time windows) and records a small number (configurable M) of per-epoch items: a compact 64-bin quantile histogram keyed by (model_family, sequence_length_bucket, batch_size_bucket), an optional flamepoint signature (top token n-gram fingerprint), and a lightweight kernel-attribution vector (per-kernel busy-time fraction for the sampled request). Samples are serialized to a columnar parquet-like compact proto and uploaded to the telemetry sink. The top-k hotpath detector consumes the atlas stream and runs a sliding-window aggregation that scores (kernel_combination, token_fingerprint) tuples by their incremental contribution to the tail (p95+/p999). Outputs are TopK reports and concise flame-snapshots suitable for on-call triage.

Why sampling: Full-trace capture is too expensive at production scale. We focused on controlled probabilistic sampling with stratification so that rare long-tail patterns are still discoverable while keeping sustained storage under existing telemetry budgets. There are knobs for sample rate, epoch size, and sequence-length stratification.

Testing and validation: Added a new benchmark suite (benchmarks/atlas_fidelity_suite) that replays representative sessions (short chat, long completion, multi-turn) and compares atlas-derived quantiles against ground-truth full-trace quantiles. The suite runs locally in CI as a smoke fidelity check and in the lab as a heavier regression test. Perf impact on the serving host was measured: sampling at 0.5% adds ~0.6ms mean CPU per request and negligible memory pressure.

Rollout plan: Feature gate turned on by default in bench clusters only. After one week of monitoring for ingestion stability and tail-detection false positives, we'll enable generation for nightly historical runs. Operator docs and dashboard tiles are included in this PR.

Notes: The description below includes commits and a short review thread. All code paths have unit tests and a small end-to-end integration test that runs the atlas reporter against a synthetic runner.

review_comments: Evan Brooks: Nice design. Two questions: (1) how do we guarantee sample representativeness across long sessions? (2) please quantify storage overhead for a 30-day retention at 0.5% sampling.

Author (Maya Chen): For long sessions we stratify by sequence_length_bucket and epoch boundaries; long sessions typically span multiple epochs so they get sampled proportionally. Storage estimate: at 0.5% sampling, our synthetic replay projects ~12GB/month for the entire lab fleet (detailed numbers in docs/benchmarks/atlas.md).
Priya Nair: The scoring function in topk_hotpath looks expensive in the worst case. Can we cap cardinality? Consider approximate heavy-hitter sketch first and exact top-k only for candidates.

Author (Maya Chen): Good call. Implemented a two-stage pipeline: lightweight Count-Min sketch for candidate selection, then exact Top-K on the candidate set. Benchmarks in the commits show sketch reduces memory by ~10x with negligible recall loss.

Daniel Ortiz: Tests look good; CI initially failed linting in epochal_atlas.py -> fixed. Also flagged a missing metric export for sample_rate; added atlas_metrics.py to expose sample_rate, sample_count, and drop_count.
Evan Brooks: Approved after sketch change and docs updates.
